Team — attaching the capacity workbook and a short summary slide. Key assumptions in the workbook (capacity_model_acme_v2.xlsx):
- Baseline active sessions: 18k/day, median seq len 512 tokens, 95th pct sessions at 1,200 tokens.

- With prefix caching (hot prefixes ~12% of tokens) and dynamic batching improvements, we simulate a 28% reduction in GPU-minutes during peak.

Quick unit-economics notes and conservative / optimistic cases:

Conservative (no additional batching, minimal caching):
- GPU cost: $3.20 / GPU-min (effective blended cost across cloud regions & reserved discounts).
- Estimated GPU-min per 1M tokens: 115 GPU-min (baseline model).
- Effective token cost: ~$0.000368 / token.
- Peak (2.5x) incremental cost multiplier: ~2.4x due to lower batching efficiency under bursty load.

Optimistic (aggressive batching + prefix/KV caching):
- Effective GPU-min per 1M tokens: 82 GPU-min (∼29% improvement).
- Effective token cost: ~$0.000262 / token.
- With caching applied to hot prefixes and warm KV caches, observed incremental cost multiplier during peak drops to ~1.6x.

Operational notes that feed pricing decision:
- Batching knobs: max batch size increase from 64→128 improves GPU utilization but risks tail latency increases; recommend adaptive batching with latency guardrails.
- Prefix caching: requires warmed cache (warm-up window ~10–20 minutes). For a 2-hour concentrated spike, caching yields most benefit when traffic has recurrent prefixes.

Ask: Laura — can you add two rows to the workbook with the conservative/optimistic token-cost outputs per 100M tokens (already in the sheet but want the rounded-dollar summary for the leadership slide). Monica — confirm rollback plan timing if we push canary scaling to reserved.

Rishi Malhotra
